# Phase equilibrium of multiple condensables {#sec-ch04}

A parcel of a planetary atmosphere can hold several vapours at once, each of which may condense: water, ammonia,
hydrogen sulfide, and the solid ammonium hydrosulfide that forms from two of them. *Saturation adjustment* moves
vapour into condensate, or back, until every condensation reaction is either at equilibrium or has no condensate
left. This chapter states those conditions and explains how kintera solves them at fixed temperature and pressure,
at fixed internal energy and volume, how it decides which condensates are present, and how it reports a cell where
the solve fails. The separate chemical-equilibrium solver, which balances reactions through equilibrium constants
from NASA polynomials, is the subject of @sec-ch05.

The nucleation reactions (@sec-ch04-nucleation) define which conditions apply. Both solvers aim at those conditions
and call the constrained least-squares step (@sec-ch04-active-set), and the warm-start and failure bookkeeping wraps
both, as shown in @fig-ch04-dependency-map.
